label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Hi Tolu, I'm in Biology 100L right now and I wanted Medicine, so this is literally my story from last year. I'll tell you everything as it is.

First, the crying. I scored 251, applied Medicine and Surgery, and when I saw Biology on the portal I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't even eat. And my mum had been telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months, so I had to beg her to stop. So whatever you're feeling since Friday, it's normal. You're not being dramatic.

Now your questions.

**Can you actually transfer?** Yes, it's real. But it is NOT easy, and nobody should accept Biology thinking it's automatic. What our level adviser told us is that you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 after 100L, AND there must be space in Medicine. The space part is the one you can't control. She said that last year about 6 people were moved into Medicine from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 people applied. So even people who do well can miss it because of the number of slots.

She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs for both JAMB and post-UTME. I don't know your school's cut-offs or what you got in post-UTME, so please check both. 268 is a very good score, but that alone doesn't tell you you're eligible. It depends on the school's own requirements.

So Kingsley saying transfer is a myth isn't true, and favour saying "just read hard" is too simple. Reading hard is necessary, but it may not be enough on its own.

**My own CGPA.** After first semester mine is 4.31. That's not 4.5, and I'm still trying. I'm not telling you this to scare you, only so you know that even someone who is working hard and doing well can be below the line. The courses in 100L are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people, so if those two are not your friends, start making peace with them now.

**Is Biology a bad course?** No. I didn't expect to say this, but I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I thought I would. In our first BIO practical we dissected toads, and one guy in my group fainted. I was fine, and that was the day I realised I actually like this thing. It also helps to know a bit of money stuff since practicals are not free: my lab coat was 6,500 naira, the dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual was extra. Not a crazy amount, but plan for it.

**What about rewriting?** Staying at home is not as easy as people say. A girl from my secondary school rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she's still at home. I'm not telling you that to say rewriting always ends like that. Plenty of people rewrite and get what they want. But it's not a guaranteed win either, and it's a long year (or years) of waiting. Rewriting is not wrong if you are really ready for it, with the plan, the discipline and the support. Just don't do it only because you're angry about the portal.

Two things I'd really do before your acceptance deadline:

1. **Go to the faculty or department and ask for the exact transfer rules for your own school.** Don't just trust forum people, including me. Ask what CGPA is needed, how many people they usually take, whether JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs matter for the transfer, and when you have to apply. Rules can be different from school to school, and my school's rules might not be yours.

2. **Ask yourself honestly: do I want Medicine, or do I just want to be "doctor" for my parents?** Only you can answer that. If it's really Medicine you want, then either path (transfer attempt or rewrite) makes sense and you can choose based on the facts. If it's more about what people will say, then Biology might be much less of a tragedy than it feels today.

Your dad and your aunty both mean well, but they're only seeing one side each. The truth is in the middle: accepting is not a guaranteed route to Medicine, and rewriting is not a guaranteed route either. You have two weeks, so use them to get real information instead of deciding from tears.

Whatever you choose, it's not the end of the world. You've got 268, which means you are not a weak student, and you'll be fine either way. Be patient with yourself, eat something, and talk to your people. If you accept and want to know more about what 100L feels like, just ask me here. I'm happy to help.
